findings: Public evidence inspected, not executed: ajent-social/go HEAD ae129822f21c51cf77975df804f668dcee6aab9d and capability catalog contracts. This planning pass ran no build/test/provider or deployment checks.

AMSL accounts, magiclink, oidc, passkey, checkout, subscription, entitlement and usage are CANDIDATE; current source is not proof of production qualification. Catalog identity.password-hashing rejects new primitive in favor of maintained implementations; identity.sessions is DISCOVERED/REFERENCE_EXISTING.
AMSL accounts is a thin person registry. AMSL tenant is deployment-instance provisioning, not organizations. AMOS owns workspace/membership/role/lifecycle policy and transaction composition.

AMSL OIDC Start/Accept inspect state and nonce but current Pending has no PKCE verifier. T3.22 is a narrow synthetic-consumer-first upstream qualification/change; maintainer security review and immutable release precede dependency pin.

AMSL passkey tests cover configured origin and ceremony consume-before-verify; current observed unit tests do not establish complete browser/provider assurance. SQL tests in accounts/oidc/passkey can skip when PostgreSQL is absent; final qualification must reject those skips.

AMSL checkout already exposes durable attempts and unknown-response recovery. Subscription currently projects one subscription per customer with status/period and CAS epoch; its event merge is not authoritative price/item/freshness reconciliation. AMOS T5.8 fetches provider state, handles replacement/multiple-subscription policy and records freshness.
AMSL usage is a bounded per-owner period counter, not immutable billable event identity, financial aggregation, provider metering or invoicing. E5 metering stays application composition.

All paths and commands in tasks are proposed executable contracts: package/test files do not yet exist. Root resolves REQUIRES dependencies and freezes public interfaces before dispatch. Planned commands are not claims of checks run.

All API mutations require real HTTP status/body and persisted-state assertions in named task tests. Browser tasks own golden plus genuine denied/edge tests; domain services remain the authority. MCP mapping is subject to root exposure schema and returns resumable proof challenges rather than privilege bypass.

Each engineering task must format touched Go files, run scoped vet/lint under root validation policy and record non-skipped results. Multi-package Go or npm builds require shared build lease and load check; commands here are scoped and none were executed.

Coding completion, merged integration, fixture qualification, real provider qualification and E16 production release are separate states. No task here authorizes production deployment, live charges or provider signup.

All later-stage contracts are provisional until prerequisite freezes; full inventory is intentional founder override of rolling-wave outline policy. No private source or private evidence is required for any public test case.
